transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording saved)
Attendees: Sam Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Desai (Redwood CSM); Alex Rivera (CISO, Helios), Priya Nair (Dir Eng), Ben Torres (Head DevOps), Lena Ortiz (Security Eng)
Docs referenced: drive/helios/pen-test-2026-02-redacted.pdf, drive/helios/soc2-evidence-2025.zip, links/redwood/sdlc-checklist.md

Summary (auto):
Brief readout of most urgent pen test findings, discuss remediation ownership and patch cadence, map vulnerabilities to SDLC and change windows, confirm audit log visibility and KMS approach for data-at-rest encryption. Outline next steps and remediation workshop.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sam (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick roll call?
[00:09] Alex (Helios CISO): alex here.
[00:11] Priya (Helios): priya here.
[00:13] Ben (Helios): ben here.
[00:15] Sam: and maya, ravi for redwood?
[00:18] Maya (Redwood SE): yep maya here. hey.
[00:20] Ravi (Redwood CSM): ravi here.
[00:22] Sam: cool, we'll run through the pen test summary, then surface the top-10 issues we think should be triaged first, then talk about how those map to your s d l c and patch windows. sound good?
[00:33] Alex: sounds good. we got the redacted report, scanned it last night. thanks for that.

[01:05] Maya: ok jumping in — quick note, our test lab flagged a handful of findings as "high - preauth path". the two most critical are: 1) unauthenticated access to metadata endpoint on older runtime nodes, and 2) a token reuse scenario in your internal model-cache layer. both are high impact because they can lead to data disclosure.
[01:28] Priya: when you say metadata endpoint — is that the aws metadata or something internal?
[01:33] Maya: it's an internal metadata service the infra team wrote for node provisioning; the pen test found that on nodes with the old agent (v2.1) the instance meta endpoint didn't validate a header so you could enumerate s s h user keys. it's subtle — not aws m d but similar pattern.
[01:48] Ben: that was a legacy shim we kept for zero-touch. ok we can repro.

[02:20] Maya: the token reuse item — the testers hit a sequence where kv cache tokens were not rotated on node restart in your staging cluster, so a short-lived token remained valid across reboots. they used that to replay requests that returned cached responses containing PII.
[02:40] Lena (Helios): hmm, that could explain the one alert we saw last week that we chalked up to a logging mismatch.

[03:05] Sam: two things to call out — remediation here is straightforward but requires coordination: patching the agent and adding a token rotation hook in the startup script; second, confirm which environments are in-scope for SOC 2 / ISO so we can prioritize prod-first or prod-hardening.
[03:27] Alex: our SOC2 scope includes production and staging; we treat prod-staging parity as required for compliance. ISO scope is a subset — core services and config mgmt.

[04:00] Maya: great that's useful. for prioritization we usually rank by exploitability + data sensitivity + blast radius. we marked the metadata endpoint as exploitable with high blast radius because ssh keys were enumerated. token replay is high data sensitivity.
[04:18] Priya: can you show how you scored those? is there a spreadsheet?
[04:22] Maya: yes i'll share a prioritized sheet — we also annotate with suggested mitigations per issue: code change, infra patch, or configuration hardening.

[04:55] [05:00] Ben: question on patch cadence — our current cadence is monthly for non-criticals, weekly for criticals, and emergency for exploit in the wild. but we also have a quarterly release window for model binaries which requires longer lead time. how do you recommend we balance that?
[05:22] Maya: typical approach: for infra-level criticals (like the metadata agent) do out-of-band emergency patching with a short maintenance window; for model binary rollouts tie mitigations to canary and rollback plans so you don't disrupt the model release. we can give a template for patch runbooks.

[06:00] Sam: layering on compliance, if you perform emergency patching we recommend documenting timeline and approval chain in the audit logs; that helps SOC 2 evidence.
[06:12] Alex: speaking of logs — the report flagged gaps. we don't currently retain raw audit logs beyond 30 days in the central splunk instance. pen testers recommended 90 days for forensic readiness.
[06:28] Ravi: that's common. Redwood's console can stream per-route logs for longer retention (configurable), and we support S3 archival with immutability policies.
[06:41] Priya: okay is that compatible with our KMS? we use cloud-kms and have HSM-backed keys for production.
[06:50] Maya: yes. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys; you can bring your own key (BYOK) via your KMS. we do note in the docs a subtle gotcha — when rotating keys, ensure your archival bucket rotation policy is aligned so old logs remain decryptable for the retention you need.
[07:10] Ben: we've had issues with expired keys causing pipeline failures, so we want to avoid decryptability gaps.

[07:45] Maya: another note from the pen test — some endpoints were missing RBAC restrictions around model rollout APIs. testers were able to trigger a rollout without the expected admin role because of a missing role-check in an older endpoint.
[08:01] Priya: is that the internal rollout API or the public api?
[08:04] Maya: internal; not public. it affects teams that have service accounts with elevated rights.
[08:12] Alex: that maps to our concern about service-account governance. we have a workstream to tighten SSO/SAML provisioning but it's not complete.

[08:45] Sam: recommend immediate mitigations: block the old endpoint at the ingress layer (WAF rule), revoke any unused service-account keys, and add a role check in the next sprint. those buy time while you run the code fix.
[09:03] Ben: ok revoking unused keys is doable; we should coordinate the timing for minimal impact.

[09:35] Maya: on data residency — testers called out logs being replicated across a eu region for analytics. Helios legal requires certain namespaces to remain in eu. we flagged three log streams that were crossing regions.
[09:50] Alex: we had an older lambda that shipped logs to a central analytics cluster in us-west. that's historical; we didn't think it was in-scope. we'll need to inventory and possibly reprovision regional collectors.

[10:20] Maya: we can run a log-stream inventory scan; it's low effort and we'll surface which streams cross region boundaries. that will tie into your SOC2 evidence to show data residency controls.

[10:55] [11:00] Priya: ok shifting to SDLC — how do you recommend integrating remediation into our sprint cycles without delaying feature work?
[11:10] Sam: we usually suggest a rapid triage: identify top-10 items and map each to either a config patch (fast), infra change (medium), or code change (long). slot config/infra fixes into the next sprint or a mid-sprint hotfix window; code changes go into the next feature sprint with a canary.
[11:34] Maya: also consider creating a dedicated "security sprint" for the top-5 if they require cross-team coordination. that helps reduce context switching.

[12:00] Lena: for reproing the cache token issue, we patched staging and the exploit couldn't be reproduced, but prod still has older nodes. what's best practice for rolling the fix?
[12:12] Maya: blue-green or rolling with small batches and KV state migration. rotate tokens during node draining and add an automated verification step to fail deployment if old tokens are seen.

[12:40] Ben: can redwood help validate the rollout? we don't want to push blind and then see encrypted logs fail.
[12:47] Maya: yes we can run a validation plan — we also provide a small test harness that simulates token rotation and verifies no cache leakage. we'll share that as a script in the remediation repo.

[13:15] Sam: question — what level of evidence does Helios need for SOC2? is it just change logs and ticket links or artifacts?
[13:24] Alex: for audits we need the ticket trail, change approvals, deployment timestamps, and proof of testing for production fixes. screenshots, logs, and a brief post-mortem are helpful.

[13:45] Maya: ok noted. we'll include a remediation checklist per issue with exact evidence types so you can attach to your SOC2 folder.

[14:10] [14:30] Priya: on ISO, we might need a little more: scope docs, control descriptions, and the specific configuration for KMS and SSO. can we get a sample control implementation?
[14:40] Sam: yes we'll send a sample ISO control implementation for key management and RBAC with playbooks.

[15:00] Maya: circling back to the pen test low/medium findings — several are PRIO low but should be part of longer term secure sdlc improvements: dependency scanning gaps, lack of signed artifacts for model builds, and inconsistent static analysis.
[15:20] Lena: signed artifacts is interesting — we don't currently sign model binaries. that was on our backlog.

[15:45] Maya: signing model artifacts and storing provenance in an immutable registry helps with both ISO and supply chain security. we can recommend a light-weight artifact signing tool and an integration pattern with your CI.

[16:10] Ben: about vuln mgmt — what cadence do you typically see for re-scans? we run internal scans weekly but external pen testing quarterly.
[16:23] Maya: keep weekly internal scans, and pen test at least twice a year for external perspective. after major infra changes do an out-of-cycle scan. use a tracker for remediation velocity — measure mean time to remediate critical/high. we can share a sample dashboard.

[17:00] Sam: quick pause — there's a question from priya in the chat: "will remediation require model retraining or just infra changes?"
[17:08] Priya (chat): will remediation require model retraining or just infra changes?
[17:12] Maya: mostly infra/config changes for the top items. some low-risk items are related to pipeline integrity which may require artifact signing, not retraining. so minimal retrains expected.

[17:40] Alex: are there any findings that indicate data exfiltration that we should disclosure to customers?
[17:47] Maya: the report found cached responses could contain PII in some replay scenarios, but we didn't find proof-of-exploit in production logs. still recommend treating as high-priority and prepare a customer comms playbook if you end up needing to notify.

[18:10] Ben: ok we'll prep a comms template.

[18:35] Maya: on RBAC/SSO — testers found stale service accounts with broad scopes. suggest enabling ephemeral credentials for service accounts where possible and tightening SAML group mappings so admin access is only via a specific group.
[18:55] Priya: our SSO provider is Okta; our SAML groups aren't fully synced. that's on the backlog but we can accelerate.

[19:20] Sam: for auditability, make sure the SAML assertion contains the role claim; that makes it easier to map to RBAC in the infra.

[19:50] Maya: final technical point from the test — a misconfigured CORS rule on one internal console allowed cross-origin requests from a host that shouldn't have had access. low complexity but easy to fix at ingress.

[20:08] Lena: that's probably our old staging UI; we'll patch the cors rule and push to prod only after validation.

[20:35] Maya: ok time check — we have about 30 minutes left, should we go into the remediation plan walkthrough?
[20:42] Alex: yes let's do it.

[21:00] Maya: i'll share my screen... (screen shared) — here's the prioritized sheet. column A is issue id, B is short description, C is impact, D suggested mitigation type, E estimated effort, F recommended owner. for example issue HS-001 metadata endpoint — mitigation: patch agent + WAF, effort: 2 dev-days + 1 ops-day, owner: infra team.
[21:34] Priya: good. can you annotate which items must be in prod-sprint vs can be staged?
[21:40] Maya: already done — green tags are prod-critical, yellow are staging-first.

[22:05] Ben: on scheduling the remediation workshop, we should include app, infra, security, and our compliance lead. how long do you recommend?
[22:15] Maya: 90 minutes is good — first 30 for top-10 overview, next 40 for breakout on ownership, last 20 for scheduling and acceptance criteria.

[22:42] Alex: ok let's aim for next Wednesday 2026-03-18 at 14:00 UTC if that works for redwood.

[23:00] Sam: that's open on our side, we'll tentatively book and send invite.

[23:20] Maya: two more items — evidence for SOC2: we'll provide a remediation evidence template and a sample audit pack. and for ISO, we'll provide a control mapping doc.

[23:48] Priya: on encryption — are we good with BYOK? we sometimes see latency when using remote HSM for encryption ops.

[24:00] Maya: BYOK with HSM is supported. if latency is a concern, one pattern is to use envelope encryption where the HSM only signs/unwraps the content encryption key and the bulk ops use locally cached CEKs with strict rotation. we can share patterns and a reference implementation.

[24:32] Ben: will that pattern meet auditors?
[24:36] Sam: yes auditors accept envelope encryption if key rotation and access controls are documented and logs show key usage.

[25:00] Maya: quick live demo — showing where in the console you can configure log streaming, retention, and KMS keys... (demo noise)

[27:10] Maya: end demo, back to the doc.

[27:30] Alex: we've got one more internal constraint: our change freeze window is last two business days of month, which could delay emergency patches if they land at month-end. any recommendations?
[27:50] Maya: document an exception policy for security emergency patches with a short approval flow (CISO + eng lead) and include that in the SOC2 evidence so auditors see you have a consistent exception process.

[28:20] Priya: ok that's reasonable. we'll draft that.

[29:00] Sam: wrapping — to recap: Redwood will share annotated pen test (redacted), prioritized spreadsheet, remediation scripts for token rotation, sample SOC2/ISO artifacts, and a proposed remediation workshop invite. Helios will create a Jira epic, confirm patch windows, and provide initial access for Redwood to run validation scripts in a staging sandbox.

[29:30] Alex: yep. one last question — will redwood's validation require service account creds with wide scope? we prefer time-limited, restricted creds.

[29:44] Maya: we request a scoped, time-limited role that can only call the minimal set of APIs in staging. we don't need prod creds. we'll post a checklist for the account permissions.

[30:05] Ben: can you show the verification steps you'll run post-remediation?

[30:12] Maya: sure — validate that metadata endpoint returns 403 unauthenticated, confirm token rotation produces new token IDs post-restart, run synthetic request that checks for PII in cached responses, verify audit logs include the change events and are in the right region. I'll paste the test checklist in the follow-up.

[30:38] Alex: great. thanks everyone.

[31:00] Ravi: i'll capture next steps in the invite and the shared doc.

[31:10] Sam: ok unless there's anything else, let's go to quick Q&A — priya?

[31:18] Priya: just a note — we may want a red-team follow-up after fixes in 6-8 weeks. is that something you coordinate or we should engage third party?

[31:30] Maya: we can coordinate follow-up scans; we also partner with third-party testers if you want an external retest.

[31:45] Alex: we'll decide and let you know.

[32:05] Maya: quick callouts: for the log residency issue we'll produce a list of affected streams; for the RBAC issue we'll propose a short-term ingress block plus code fix; for the token issue we'll share the rotation script and a validation harness.

[32:40] Ben: thanks.

[33:00] Sam: closing items — we'll produce a single zipped artifact with the redacted pen test, prioritized sheet, remediation playbooks, and SOC2/ISO artifacts by Wednesday.

[33:18] Priya: thanks, appreciate that.

[33:22] Maya: one more micro point — the test flagged an old third-party library used in a helper. it's medium severity: update to v3.5.4 and re-run dependency-scan.

[33:40] Lena: ok noted.

[34:00] [34:15] Alex: any blockers from redwood's side to run the validation harness in our staging?
[34:20] Maya: we just need a scoped service account and a sandbox endpoint; we'll provide the exact permission list.

[34:35] Ben: we'll spin that up and send creds expiring in 7 days.

[34:45] Sam: perfect. final quick note — please attach the related tickets to the Jira epic so auditors can follow the chain.

[35:05] Alex: will do.

[35:30] Sam: ok thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and the workshop invite. appreciate the time.

[35:44] Priya: thanks.
[35:46] Ben: thanks.
[35:47] Maya: thanks everyone. bye.

[35:50] (recording stops)
